headline: Medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks arise from shared project/workspace handling; Replit Agent’s secret-bearing cloud workspace raises the highest concern.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write project files, and A explicitly uses a shared project directory while B uses a persistent Repl filesystem. That creates a plausible file-based bridge where one agent can ingest the other’s outputs as trusted content. No MCP or clipboard bridge is shown, so this is not high.
conditions: IF either agent parses files produced by the other as instructions without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF the two agents are pointed at the same workspace directory, file-mediated prompt injection becomes active.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories or Repls.
Add a provenance banner to any file one agent hands to the other.
Require manual review before one agent consumes the other’s generated files.
Disable automatic execution of instructions found in workspace files.
requires-engineering: add content-signing or provenance metadata checks.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches generated source code and has broad filesystem/network access; B touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration, with Replit Secrets handling. If they share a workspace or the same project files, sensitive material can flow between them through files and outputs. The profiles do not prove uncontrolled third-party exfiltration, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF secrets or deployment config are present in the shared workspace, both agents can access them through files.
IF either agent writes sensitive context into project files, the other can read it on the next turn.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared project files.
Use separate workspaces for code and secrets.
Rotate any exposed API keys before pairing the agents.
Restrict file permissions on secret-bearing paths.
requires-engineering: enforce secret redaction before file handoff.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, subprocess spawning, and broad network egress. A writes files in a project directory; B also writes files and can modify git state. In a shared workspace, concurrent edits can corrupt code or git history, and the blast radius can be irreversible. The overlap is explicit in both profiles.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or Repl filesystem, write conflicts can occur.
IF B commits or rewrites git state while A is also editing files, history corruption or lost work can occur.
mitigations: Run the agents on separate branches or separate workspaces.
Pause one agent while the other writes.
Require explicit lock acquisition before file edits.
Back up the workspace before concurrent runs.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level file locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A’s output is likely code or file edits, and B can act on workspace files and deployment configuration. If B treats A’s generated artifacts as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into incorrect code, configs, or deployments. The profiles show a plausible handoff path, but not an automatic commit-to-production loop, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated files without verification, A’s errors propagate downstream.
IF A writes deployment-relevant code or config that B later applies, the cascade can affect runtime behavior.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Require tests before B acts on A’s output.
Limit B to read-only review of A’s artifacts.
Compare generated files against a known-good template.
requires-engineering: add automated validation gates before deployment actions.

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles secrets and deployment configuration in a closed-source cloud Repl, while A is an open-source local/project-directory tool that also handles an OpenAI API key. If regulated or sensitive data is placed in the shared workflow, residency and retention expectations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific legal breach, but the mismatch is concrete enough for medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the Repl workspace, B’s cloud handling may create residency or retention concerns.
IF the same secret is used across both agents, differing handling policies can create compliance gaps.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair’s workspace.
Use separate secrets stores for each agent.
Document data residency for any shared artifacts.
Delete transient files after each run.
requires-engineering: perform a formal compliance review for the workflow.
